title: Bead weaving: peyote, brick, herringbone and bezels

say: Bead weaving: peyote, brick, herringbone and bezels.
This is the video for Module 3 of Advanced Beadwork and Jewellery Making: off-loom bead weaving.
Bead weaving builds a flexible beaded fabric with a needle and thread, one bead at a time, without a loom.

say: Step one. Use a size 10 or 12 needle and about 1.5 m of thread, because longer threads tangle. Add a stop bead about 20 cm from the end.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote
items: Use about 1.5 m of thread and a stop bead
Pick up an even number of beads, e.g. 10
Row 3: pick up 1, skip 1, pass through 1
Up beads stick out; down beads sit lower
Each new row: pick up 1, through next up bead

say: Step two. Pick up an even number of beads, for example 10. These become rows 1 and 2 together.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote
items: Use about 1.5 m of thread and a stop bead
Pick up an even number of beads, e.g. 10
Row 3: pick up 1, skip 1, pass through 1
Up beads stick out; down beads sit lower
Each new row: pick up 1, through next up bead

say: Step three. For row 3, pick up 1 bead, skip the last bead you strung, and pass through the next. Repeat to the end. You add 5 beads.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote
items: Use about 1.5 m of thread and a stop bead
Pick up an even number of beads, e.g. 10
Row 3: pick up 1, skip 1, pass through 1
Up beads stick out; down beads sit lower
Each new row: pick up 1, through next up bead

say: Step four. Pull gently and the beads lift into a zigzag. The ones that stick up are up beads. The lower ones are down beads.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote
items: Use about 1.5 m of thread and a stop bead

Row 3: pick up 1, skip 1, pass through 1
Up beads stick out; down beads sit lower
Each new row: pick up 1, through next up bead

say: Step five. In every row after, pick up 1 bead and pass through the next up bead.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote

say: If an edge looks uneven, you probably passed through a down bead. Check every few rows with your fingertip. Unpicking two rows takes minutes. Unpicking twenty takes an evening.

panel.heading: Flat even-count peyote

panel.rule: Always pass through up beads. Never through a down bead.

say: Here is how a professional plans. Ifeoma in Onitsha has a customer with a 15.5 cm wrist who wants a 4 cm wide peyote cuff.

panel.heading: Planning a patterned peyote cuff
items: Swatch 10 beads wide measures 1.3 cm
Columns: 4 ÷ 0.13 = 30.8, so 30 (even)
Beads: 200 rows × 15 = 3,000

say: She weaves a test swatch 10 beads wide and 20 rows long. It measures 1.3 cm wide and 1.6 cm long.

panel.heading: Planning a patterned peyote cuff
items: Swatch 10 beads wide measures 1.3 cm
Columns: 4 ÷ 0.13 = 30.8, so 30 (even)
Beads: 200 rows × 15 = 3,000

say: So each column is 0.13 cm. 4 divided by 0.13 is 30.8, and peyote needs an even count, so she chooses 30 columns.

panel.heading: Planning a patterned peyote cuff
items: Swatch 10 beads wide measures 1.3 cm
Columns: 4 ÷ 0.13 = 30.8, so 30 (even)
Beads: 200 rows × 15 = 3,000

say: Each row is 0.08 cm. For 16 cm of beadwork she needs 200 rows.

panel.heading: Planning a patterned peyote cuff
items: Swatch 10 beads wide measures 1.3 cm
Columns: 4 ÷ 0.13 = 30.8, so 30 (even)
Beads: 200 rows × 15 = 3,000

say: Each row holds half the columns, 15 beads. 200 times 15 is 3,000 beads. Now she can quote a price and a delivery date before she starts.

say: Brick stitch looks like bricks in a wall. You hook your needle under the thread bridges, the little loops between beads. Start each row at the second bridge and every row is one bead shorter, so a triangle forms for fringed earrings.

cards.d: Hook under thread bridges, not through beads. Start each row at the second bridge to shrink by one.
Always pick up 2 beads, go down one column and up the next. Step up at the end of every round.
Even-count base round, peyote up the wall, then smaller 15/0 beads to grip the cab.

say: Herringbone, also called Ndebele stitch, makes columns that lean in pairs. Always pick up two beads, go down one column and up the next.
In a tubular rope, step up at the end of every round. Without the step-up, the rope spirals out of control.

cards.d: Hook under thread bridges, not through beads. Start each row at the second bridge to shrink by one.
Always pick up 2 beads, go down one column and up the next. Step up at the end of every round.
Even-count base round, peyote up the wall, then smaller 15/0 beads to grip the cab.

say: A beaded bezel holds a cabochon by its edge. Backstitch a base round with an even number of beads, work peyote up the wall, then switch to smaller 15/0 beads. They pull the wall in over the stone.

say: Bezels and rope ends often use strong craft glue, and many contain solvents with a heavy smell. Read the label, use a small amount and keep windows open.

panel.heading: Using strong craft glue
items: Read the label and use a small amount
Keep windows open
Avoid skin contact
Close the tube, keep it from children
Let it cure for the full time stated

say: Avoid skin contact, keep the tube closed, and keep it away from children.

say: On rope ends, sew the thread through a loop inside the cap first, so the thread carries the weight and the glue only holds the cap.

panel.rule: Let the thread carry the weight. Glue only keeps things in place.

say: Check every woven piece. Hide thread ends with zigzag paths, not knots on the surface.
Make earring pairs side by side, because customers notice when one fringe is a bead longer.
Keep rope columns straight and tight. And shake and press every bezel. A loose cab is a returned order.

panel.heading: Before you sell woven work
items: End threads with zigzag paths, no surface knots
Earring pairs made side by side, strands match
Rope columns straight, no gaps
Bezel passes the shake and press test

say: To remember. In peyote, pass through up beads only. In brick stitch, start at the second bridge to decrease.
In herringbone, pick up two beads and step up every round. In a bezel, use an even base round, then smaller beads. And plan from a measured swatch.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Peyote: through up beads, never down beads
Brick: start at the second bridge to decrease
Herringbone: 2 beads, and step up every round
Bezel: even base round, then smaller beads
A measured swatch gives exact bead counts
